problem: Routing queries to language models based on difficulty is hard to scale because routers are fixed to a small set of models and can't adapt when new models appear or cost constraints change.
approach: SCOPE predicts cost and performance of models by retrieving how similar models behave on related problems, trained with RL, rather than using fixed model names, allowing dynamic routing decisions.
contribution: Achieves up to 25.7% accuracy boost when prioritizing performance or up to 95.1% cost reduction when prioritizing efficiency, adapting flexibly to user needs.

problem: Distributional RL works in 1D but extending to multivariate return distributions is hard because common metrics don't generalize naturally or lose tractability.
approach: SDRL lifts one-dimensional divergences to multivariate settings via projections onto random directions, proving Bellman contraction for uniform slicing and maximum-slicing variants.
contribution: Provides tractable multivariate distributional RL supporting Wasserstein, Cramér, and MMD divergences with theoretical contraction guarantees.

problem: Multi-agent debate for LLMs shows promise but only helps in certain regimes; symmetric debate dynamics are neutral in expectation, making majority voting often preferable.
approach: LASE uses a leader-centric asymmetric architecture that selectively engages debate only when interaction amplifies informative signals, defaulting to simple aggregation otherwise.
contribution: Achieves multi-agent performance with near single-agent token cost, substantially improving efficiency over static debate and voting baselines.

problem: Sparse attention for 2D images requires balancing spatial locality with hardware-efficient memory access patterns, but handcrafted patterns often cause uncoalesced GPU memory access.
approach: HilbertA reorders image tokens along a Hilbert curve to convert spatial neighborhoods into contiguous memory segments and shifts attention windows across layers for cross-tile communication.
contribution: Achieves up to 4.16× attention acceleration and 1.44× end-to-end speedup on Flux.1-dev and up to 2.30× attention acceleration with 1.57× faster time-to-first-token on Qwen3-VL-8B.

problem: Understanding how stochastic optimization methods behave when step sizes are too large is hard; it's unclear which adaptive methods are truly more robust than SGD.
approach: Analyzes sensitivity of optimization methods to step size by identifying a key quantity describing performance degradation, showing this directly impacts suboptimality bounds.
contribution: Provides theoretical evidence that adaptive methods like SPS and NGN are more robust than SGD, with bounds qualitatively mirroring actual performance across step sizes.

problem: LLM agents are acquiring capabilities relevant to biosecurity tasks like DNA design and synthesis screening, but measuring these dual-use abilities is challenging.
approach: ABC-Bench provides benchmark tasks measuring LLM agent capabilities on benign and dual-use biology: liquid handling code, DNA design, and synthesis screening evasion.
contribution: All tested LLM agents outperformed median expert human baseline on all three tasks; OpenAI o4-mini-high successfully assembled DNA with expected sequences on wet-lab robots.

problem: Approximating loss function curvature at scale is hard; existing methods ignore curvature constraints from weight-space symmetries that are invariant to loss.
approach: Analytically averages over group actions preserving loss to construct structured Hessian approximations from single gradients, with user-specified symmetry groups controlling accuracy-cost trade-offs.
contribution: Recovers Shampoo/Muon-like curvature estimates for specific symmetry choices and enables tractable second-order optimization on language models.

problem: Vision Transformers produce unstable attribution maps with structured artifacts from patch embeddings and attention routing, limiting pixel-level explanation quality.
approach: DAVE decomposes input gradients by exploiting ViT architecture to isolate locally equivariant components while suppressing architecture-induced artifacts.
contribution: Produces robust, precise, and class-consistent attribution maps outperforming prior methods on localization, faithfulness, and user studies.

problem: Knowledge transfer via distillation and weak-to-strong generalization appear disparate; a unified theory explaining when and why transfer works across regimes is missing.
approach: Establishes unified spectral analysis of SGD dynamics in high-dimensional linear regression, characterizing KT via spectral horizon expansion in KD and spectral denoising in W2S.
contribution: Reveals efficacy is governed by interplay between implicit regularization and heterogeneous spectral learning speeds, unifying seemingly different transfer phenomena.

problem: Low-bit weight-only quantization degrades quality on generative tasks because block-wise PTQ omits the unembedding layer and uses MSE, misaligning token probabilities.
approach: LFQ quantizes the final block by minimizing cross-entropy between FP and quantized logits, aligning token probability distributions at the logit level.
contribution: Consistently improves accuracy on complex generation tasks while maintaining parity with FP baselines on language modeling and understanding.

problem: MoE inference under memory constraints requires caching only a small subset of experts; uncached experts fetched from slow storage cause frequent evictions and I/O overhead.
approach: ReMoE fine-tunes the router to bias toward recently selected experts, increasing temporal expert reuse and matching cache locality constraints without adding computation.
contribution: Improves expert reuse by 26% while maintaining performance; achieves 1.77-1.99× decode speedup on real systems with different expert offloading strategies.

problem: Data markets struggle to price data appropriately when value follows AI scaling laws, where buyers have diminishing returns as data volume increases.
approach: Analyzes offline and online mechanism design for continuous data allocation with scaling-law-based valuations, proposing two-stage algorithms combining upfront production and adaptive expansion.
contribution: Characterizes profit-optimal mechanisms and shows simple two-stage algorithm achieves constant-factor approximation to offline optimum under demand uncertainty.

problem: Proving program termination is undecidable and difficult; generating sound loop bounds that guarantee termination is a hard verification challenge.
approach: LIFT uses LLMs to generate loop bounds within a guess-and-check workflow coupled with formal validation that guarantees reported terminations and refutes invalid bounds.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing termination verification tools on public benchmarks.

problem: 4-bit activations and 8-bit gradients in distributed LLM training cause slow convergence or accuracy loss due to inadequate quantization precision.
approach: AGoQ combines layer-aware activation quantization allocating appropriate bit-widths per layer type and precision-preserving 8-bit gradient All-Reduce communication.
contribution: Reduces memory by up to 52% and achieves up to 1.34× training speedup compared to Megatron-LM, COAT, and DeepSpeed on 8B-32B models.

problem: Portrait pose transfer requires preserving identity while following pose instructions, and existing methods struggle with extensive annotation and suboptimal optimization objectives.
approach: PortraitRL uses multi-objective LVLM-based rewards and proposes NaSPO, a novel RL algorithm identifying positive/negative samples automatically without annotation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with significant improvements in detail preservation and editing accuracy.

problem: Diffusion language models are slower to train from scratch than autoregressive models despite their parallel generation benefits.
approach: Studies AR-to-dLM conversion preserving AR weight distributions via block-wise attention and proposes position-dependent token masking to reduce mask distribution gap.
contribution: Efficient-DLM-8B achieves +5.4% higher accuracy with 4.7× higher throughput than AR models and superior accuracy-throughput trade-offs over dLM baselines.

problem: Offline RL single-step TD learning suffers from bootstrapping error accumulation over long horizons; action-chunked methods help but restrict policy to open-loop sequences.
approach: CGQ guides a single-step critic by regularizing it toward a chunk-based critic trained with temporally extended backups, preserving fine-grained value propagation.
contribution: Achieves tighter critic optimality bounds than single-step or action-chunked TD alone, with strong performance on long-horizon OGBench tasks.

problem: Balancing inference quality and cost requires independent decisions via model routing and test-time scaling, but this decoupled design limits adaptability and creates discrete performance changes.
approach: UniScale unifies routing and TTS in one optimization space, formulating adaptive unified inference scaling as a contextual bandit problem solved via LinUCB.
contribution: Delivers fine-grained and consistently better quality-cost trade-offs across diverse, dynamic inference scenarios.

problem: Structure-based drug design is difficult without feedback mechanisms; one-shot generative models lack the iterative refinement that human experts use.
approach: K-BTS formalizes iterative drug design as a dynamic hierarchical multi-armed bandit using bi-level Thompson sampling with chemical rules guiding LLM generation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art Top-1 average docking score on CrossDocked2020 with smooth, monotonic convergence.

problem: LLM agents fail at multi-agent coordination even when cooperation is costless and trivially optimal, but the causes of failure are unclear.
approach: Builds a turn-based environment with zero strategic complexity and uses causal decomposition to separate cooperation failures from competence failures.
contribution: Shows stronger models don't necessarily cooperate better; targeted interventions like explicit protocols roughly double performance of competence-limited models.

problem: Euler-Maruyama time discretization in BSDE methods for PDEs introduces intrinsic bias; high-order schemes eliminate bias but reintroduce second-order derivatives and overhead.
approach: Provides principled analysis of EM-induced loss bias and proposes unbiased, second-order-free training framework preserving BSDE computational advantages.
contribution: Achieves unbiased training without explicit Hessian evaluations while maintaining BSDE efficiency for high-dimensional PDE solving.

problem: Self-supervised learning faces tension between semantic understanding and reconstruction; semantic methods lack spatial grounding while reconstruction methods yield weaker semantics.
approach: STELLAR factorizes visual features into semantic concepts and spatial distributions, enabling augmentation alignment on sparse tokens while maintaining reconstruction.
contribution: As few as 16 sparse tokens achieve both high-quality reconstruction (2.60 FID) and strong semantic transfer (79.10% ImageNet accuracy).

problem: Static LLM alignment becomes brittle as policies evolve over time due to cultural shifts and regulatory changes, creating an alignment-reality gap hard to audit or fix.
approach: TRACE transforms re-alignment into structured optimization over existing data via triaging, computing alignment impact scores, and executing updates with hybrid objectives.
contribution: Robustly re-aligns models on synthetic benchmarks and PKU-SafeRLHF dataset without fresh annotation or degrading general utility.

problem: Merging multiple LoRA adapters is computationally expensive; naive subspace factorizations make the merge step a primary latency bottleneck.
approach: CircuMerge uses shared circulant transforms to align all tasks in a common coordinate system, enabling efficient sketch-based sampling and reconstruction.
contribution: Reduces merging time by at least 44% compared to state-of-the-art while matching or exceeding optimal accuracy across vision and language benchmarks.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs leads to unintended out-of-distribution generalization; modifying training data is often impractical.
approach: CAFT uses interpretability tools to ablate undesired concept directions via linear projections during fine-tuning without modifying training data.
contribution: Reduces misaligned responses by 10× on emergent misalignment without degrading performance on training distribution.

problem: Standard MoE aggregation via weighted summation limits expert combinations; scaling performance while managing routing overhead remains challenging.
approach: DAG-MoE replaces weighted-summation with structural aggregation using a lightweight module learning optimal aggregation structure among selected experts.
contribution: Consistently improves performance in pretraining and fine-tuning, surpassing traditional MoE baselines.

problem: Video anomaly understanding relies on sparse cues and suffers from observational aliasing where static sampling fails to disambiguate distinct events.
approach: Anom-π reconceptualizes VAU as active decision-making using interleaved policy optimization with temporal operators and interactive direct preference optimization.
contribution: With only 2B parameters, significantly outperforms state-of-the-art large-scale VAU models in complex scenarios.

problem: Linear recurrent networks work well in partially observable RL but lack theoretical justification for their effectiveness.
approach: Constructs and analyzes two linear filters: one exactly reproducing belief-vector logits under deterministic HMMs and one achieving vanishing state-decoding error.
contribution: Provides theoretical justification showing linear filters serve as sufficient statistics for optimal policy learning and reduce state ambiguity.

problem: Domain generalization methods overlook uncertainty quantification; combining ensembles and distillation for domain generalization is non-trivial and unexplored.
approach: DomED investigates ensemble and distillation strategies for domain generalization with data allocation training teachers on distinct domains and distillation on unseen domains.
contribution: Achieves competitive accuracies and substantially improved uncertainty estimates across multiple domain generalization benchmarks.

problem: 2D generative world models exhibit physical inconsistencies like morphing or vanishing objects due to mixing ego-motion and environmental dynamics within the image plane.
approach: FR3D predicts persistent 3D latent representation and explicitly decouples scene evolution from agent trajectory, using teacher-student distillation from foundation models.
contribution: Strong performance for future dynamic 3D reconstruction from monocular observations across datasets, maintaining consistency 2 seconds into the future.

problem: Interactive world models typically lack 3D representation, limiting spatial memory to temporal context windows and preventing 3D-consistent generation.
approach: PERSIST simulates evolution of latent 3D scene with environment, camera, and renderer, enabling persistent spatial memory and consistent geometry.
contribution: Substantially improves spatial memory, 3D consistency, and long-horizon stability; enables 3D environment editing and fine-grained geometry-aware control.

problem: Solving PDEs under extremely sparse observations (as low as 3%) is difficult; inference efficiency at high resolutions is limited and accuracy degrades severely.
approach: Di-BiLPS combines VAE for dimensionality reduction, latent diffusion for uncertainty, and contrastive learning with PDE-informed denoising in latent space.
contribution: Achieves SOTA performance under extremely sparse inputs while substantially reducing computational cost and enabling zero-shot super-resolution.

problem: Time series reasoning requires deciding what to inspect when evidence spans full series or appears in short intervals; existing methods encode entire series into fixed representation.
approach: ARTIST formulates time-series reasoning as sequential decision problem interleaving reasoning with adaptive segment selection via controller-reasoner architecture.
contribution: Improves average accuracy by 6.46 percentage points over strongest baseline; largest gains on rare event localization and multi-segment reasoning tasks.

problem: Modeling TCR-pMHC recognition is constrained by sparse paired data relative to abundant unpaired sequences, limiting existing methods.
approach: DecoderTCR uses masked language model framework with compositional curriculum pre-training and Iterative Entropy-Guided Refinement for non-autoregressive decoding.
contribution: Achieves 0.96 AUROC for zero-shot pMHC binding prediction and 0.76 AUROC for epitope-specific TCR recognition; wet-lab screening validates predictions.

problem: Large-step inference in diffusion ODEs faces a contractivity trap where efficient inference favors large steps but aggressive steps undermine stability certificates.
approach: SteinDiff introduces step-wise inference-time stabilization via Stein-derived corrections with geometry-aware residual correction mechanism and closed-form coefficient.
contribution: Mitigates severe artifacts and improves generative quality across large-step inference settings.

problem: Open-domain multimodal document retrieval over interconnected corpora requires adapting reasoning to context and recovering intelligently from failures.
approach: Failure is Feedback casts retrieval as sequential decision process with history-aware backtracking leveraging failed traversal context and cost-aware orchestration.
contribution: Enables dynamic trade-offs between accuracy and inference costs, escalating to intensive LLM reasoning only when failure justifies investment.

problem: Model soups require supervised learning; extending them to self-supervised learning is unexplored.
approach: Self-Soupervision enables soups on unlabeled data by cooking ingredients from diverse SSL algorithms and data sources including shifted or corrupted data.
contribution: Boosts robustness by +3.5% on ImageNet-C and +7% on LAION-C; mixes diverse SSL algorithms (MAE, MoCoV3, MMCR, LeJEPA) into better soups than single ingredients.

problem: Estimating first and second moments for adaptive optimizers like Adam consumes substantial memory, limiting scalability for large neural networks.
approach: IO-Adam rethinks moment estimation from gradient computation perspective, tracking input and output gradients instead of finding low-rank approximations.
contribution: Reduces memory usage by up to 30% while preserving or improving performance compared to standard Adam.

problem: Large Vision Language Models suffer from language bias, producing answers without relying on visual evidence due to lack of quantitative measure of visual information contribution.
approach: VIG measures prediction uncertainty reduction from visual input at sample and token levels, enabling VIG-guided selective training prioritizing visually informative data.
contribution: Improves visual grounding and mitigates language bias with superior performance using significantly reduced supervision.

problem: Low-complexity image compression must balance fidelity and realism under computational constraints; existing approaches struggle with this trade-off.
approach: Re2IC uses saliency-guided region partitioning and wavelet-Wasserstein distortion for frequency-decomposed perceptual optimization.
contribution: Outperforms generative codecs like HiFiC while using less than 1% of decoding cost; WA-WD metric achieves 94.6% Pearson correlation with human preference.
